title: Portal organisations and memberships
description: Organisations, the roles people hold in them, and a sign-up (portal plan P2.1; spec §Tenancy). The organisation is the tenant, its type decides what the SSO rule does with a person who belongs to it (F10, D2207), and a person's role lives in the membership and never in the sign-in token: a role in a token is a role only the identity provider can take away. Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_orgs.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

organisation.description: One organisation, as the API answers it to a member of it and, for the operations team, to anybody (P2.1).

id.description: The organisation's id. It is opaque and minted here: nothing outside the portal has a meaning for it, and it is not a Firebase project id or a domain.

name.description: The organisation's name as its members see it. It is text and not an identifier: two organisations may share one, and renaming is a later task's.

type.description: What kind of tenant this is, set once and never moved. Operations and reseller organisations are the ones the sign-in rule follows: a person who belongs to one is refused by email sign-in for any request that uses that membership (F10, D2207).

terms.description: The terms of service this organisation's sign-up accepted, or null for an organisation nobody signed up to — the operations organisation, seeded as an invitation (P2.2). Null is not an empty acceptance: it says there is no record, which is a different thing from a record with no version.

reseller_id.description: The reseller organisation that created this customer organisation on its behalf (D2191), or null when no reseller did. It is a link rather than a parent — operations can relink a customer (P6.1) — and it is what a reseller's customer list and accrual are read from.

created_at.description: When the organisation was created, in UTC. It is the organisation's instant and not the membership's: a person who joins a year later is a member of an organisation that has existed for a year.

terms.description: One acceptance of the terms of service, recorded at sign-up (D2199, P2.1's TestSignUpRecordsTermsAcceptance). The version is kept beside the instant because the terms change and the record has to say which wording was agreed to.

version.description: The version of the terms the person accepted, as the terms themselves spell it. It is not a date: a wording that is corrected without changing what it says keeps its version.

accepted_at.description: When the acceptance happened, in UTC, which is the sign-up's instant.

membership.description: One person's place in one organisation. The account itself is a Firebase Auth user; nothing about the person is copied out of the provider's answer, so this is the whole of what the portal knows about who belongs where.

organisation_id.description: The organisation this membership is in: an organisation's shape does not carry its members, because a member of one organisation is not told the membership list of another.

uid.description: The Firebase Auth uid this membership is bound to. It is written at the first sign-in of the invited address (F40): before that an invitation knows an address and not a person.

email.description: The address the identity carries, as Firebase Auth reports it. Invitations are compared against it, both sides folded by access.Member (F10), which is the only folding the two sides share.

role.description: What this person may decide in this organisation. Owners and admins are who may bind, buy, invite, reveal and delete (D2195); a member reads the organisation's screens and decides nothing in the portal. The role is per organisation: the same person is an owner of one and a member of another.

created_at.description: When the person joined, in UTC — the invitation's acceptance, or the sign-up that created the organisation.

last_used_at.description: When this person last worked in this organisation, or null while they never have. It is what the switcher lands them on (spec §Tenancy, P2.1's TestLastUsedOrg), and null is not a time: a membership nobody selected is not one selected at the epoch.

create.description: A sign-up's request (P2.1). The account is the caller's own sign-in and the type is customer: only operations creates a reseller organisation (D2191, P6.1), and nothing in the body can ask for one.

name.description: The name the person gives the organisation they are creating.
